locations.rationale: Member call `service.execute(" Ada ")` in run_demo; `service` is deduced as example::Service from build_service's return type, so the token resolves to Service::execute. No overloads exist.

Out-of-line definition token in `std::string Service::execute(const std::string& name)`; the qualified definition name resolves to the in-class declaration in service.h and lies outside the declaration range.

records.rationale: The fixture consists of service.h, service.cpp, and main.cpp; both translation units include only service.h. Exactly two identifier tokens outside the declaration range resolve to Service::execute: the qualified out-of-line definition in service.cpp and the member call in main.cpp. The `Service` qualifier and receiver tokens resolve to the class, not the method, and are not usages. There are no other exact-name candidates, no overloads, and no C++ import/export binding tokens, so the reference policy adds no optional locations. definitionUsage is the URI-sorted first required location (main.cpp sorts before service.cpp). All positions are UTF-16 code-unit offsets over pure-ASCII lines.
